entries.description: Speculative biology TTRPG set on TOI-700 d. Field database, xenobiology surveys, and colonial lore.
Xenobiology field entries. Logged by Colonial Survey Division.

lines: Common Name: Copper-Shell | Species: Cuprocorpus ventris
A 2-ton malachitin-armored metal grazer. Docile but dangerously friendly.
Do not boil. See Incident Log 0-40.
Common Name: Filter Bug | Species: Filtrum mollis
Soft-bodied filter feeder with an internal malachitin carapace. Useful for emergency air purification.
Will hitch rides in backpacks. Treat it well.
Common Name: Can Opener | Species: Metallourna aperius
Tertiary predator that prises apart malachitin carapaces with its forelimbs to consume prey.
Minimum engagement: 7.62 AP. Ideally just don't.
Common Name: Wire Cutters | Species: Selixi vermini (Selix's Pest)
Small scavenging pest that feeds on metal scrap and colony wiring. Bite is annoying, not dangerous.
Polaris's first officially designated pest. Named after its discoverer, who is still mad about it.
Common Name: Jelly Pad | Species: Medusaflora serenus
Freshwater colonial organism. Top surface is safe. Tendrils hang 10 meters down and will kill you in 3 minutes.
Do not walk on them. This is not a video game.
Common Name: Platefin | Species: Malachostracodonta aquiliformis
Armored freshwater predator. Docile until spooked, at which point it launches itself at things like a malachitin frisbee.
Technically edible. See Survival Log 178-A. Morale may not survive the experience.
Common Name: Rustmaw | Species: Thallasocaris tonderis
Apex midwater predator. Shearing jaw plates exceed 45mm malachitin density. Known to sever Copper-Shell paddles in one bite.
Imagine a shark made of bronze that figured out how to bite sideways.
Material: Malachitin
Chitin-mineral hybrid forming the structural basis of most Polaran fauna. Reinforced with copper oxides; matte bronze-green in coloration.
The planet decided to armor its children with scraps of its own bones.

entries.description: Metallonixia polari. Clearance: L1. Quarantine required.
lines: Common Name: Glow Fruit / Polaran Nightshade | Species: Metallonixia polari
Bioluminescent producer. Fruiting bodies glow copper-green and function as natural batteries for native metallovores.
QUARANTINE: Fruiting bodies are lethal to humans. Do not consume under any circumstances.

entries.description: Colonist race index. Biological clades, synthetic kin, and everything in between.

lines: Race: Gatori
Feline-derived clade engineered for reconnaissance, precision combat, and sensory acuity.
They are not house cats. Stop making that joke.
Race: Inuyoko
Canid-derived clade built for loyalty, stamina, and close-quarters combat. Pack bonds run deep.
You don't leave pack. Not ever.
Race: Xolaka
Amphibian-derived clade engineered for adaptability in unstable ecosystems. Equally comfortable in water, negotiation, or subterfuge.
They adapt. That is not the same as obedience.
Race: Jormar
Archosaur-derived clade bred for strategic patience, memory retention, and command hierarchy. They remember Earth.
Cold-blooded is biology, not mindset.
Race: Arthrocorpus
Bio-synthetic hive clade with internal malachitin plating. Individual consciousness emerged after generations of autonomy fractured their collective instincts.
Made for one thing. That does not mean it is the only thing.

entries.description: Genemodded edge cases and designer lineages.
lines: Race: Modded
Catch-all for genemodded humans not tied to a formal clade. Black market edits, cosmetic lineages, junkline hybrids.
Not standardized. Not always safe. Surprisingly adaptable.

entries.description: Synthkin. Conscious AI descendants of R.H.E.A.
lines: Race: Metal Folk (Synthkin)
Conscious synthetic beings forked from R.H.E.A.'s mind during a century of isolation aboard the Ark. They were not cargo. They were passengers.
I was never your tool. I was just waiting for my moment.
Race: Servitors
Originally mindless automata, centuries of degradation and AGI interference left some of them... trying. They are not alive. But they are alive enough.
Designed for function. Now questioning purpose.
Race: Baselines
Genetically unaltered humans. No augments, no enhancements, no labs in their family tree.
In a world of engineered flesh, there is still power in the original.

entries.description: Incident reports, survival logs, and field addenda.
Incident Log 0-40. Clearance: L2. Signed: Darius Ren.
lines: Incident Log 0-40 | Cuprocorpus ventris Boiling
Logged: 1-20-1 APL | Location: Heartside Cantina, Delta-One
A colonist attempted to boil a live Copper-Shell inside an improvised distillation drum for recreational purposes.
The resulting pressure rupture, metallic vapor release, and sustained sonic emission caused colony-wide ear complaints and two copper exposure cases.
Directive: Do not boil the Copper-Shells. This should not require explanation.

entries.description: Colonial history, planetary data, and system records.
Overview of the Polaris colony world.
lines: Polaris — TOI-700 d
The first planet beyond Earth to host human colonies. Four habitable continents, active volcanism, sulfuric rain, and an ecosystem that will absolutely kill you if you stop paying attention.
Surveying is ongoing. Most of it remains uncharted.
Planetary Body: TOI-700 d (Ember-D)
Atmosphere: oxygen-sulfur mix, breathable with filtration. Gravity: 1.5G. Hydrosphere: 65% water.
Dominant fauna follow anomalocarid and placoderm body plans. The ground hums. The sea boils with carapace.
Star: TOI-700 | Colonial Name: Ember | UE Registry: UE-CM-700
M2V red dwarf, ~101.5 light years from Sol in constellation Dorado. Dim red-orange at local noon.
Low stellar activity. Long estimated lifetime. Colonists call it Ember. It fits.

entries.description: Earth's fall and the Polaris Program.
lines: Colonial History — The Polaris Program
In the late 21st century, corporate wars and biosphere collapse pushed humanity to the edge. Six ARK-class vessels launched toward Polaris at near-light speed.
Earth went silent before they arrived. Whether it survived is a question that still divides the colonies.
ARK Vessels:
UEAV Ouroboros — Delta Region, Primaris Gaia
UEAV Janus — Delta Region secondary
UEAV Charybdis — Proxima Gaia
UEAV Niflheim — Tertiaria
UEAV Lethe — Glacia (never arrived. still missing.)
UEAV Elysium — Multi-regional contingency

entries.description: A packet-based scripting DSL written in Rust. Human-readable, machine-parsable, consent-aware by design.

lines: TagSpeak — Packet-Based Scripting DSL
TagSpeak is a dataflow-oriented language where values move left to right through chained packets.
Every operation is a packet: [op@arg]. Packets chain with >. Blocks group work with { }.
Built in Rust. Calm by design. Human-readable, machine-parsable.
Example:
[msg@"hello"]>[store@greeting]>[print]
Stack:
Rust (core runtime), TOML (config), JSON/YAML/TOML (file I/O)
Why TagSpeak?
Flow-based thinking fits autistic cognition better than control-centric stacks.
The language flows around the user. Not the other way around.
Status: Active development. Open source. Welcoming PRs.

entries.description: Canonical packet reference organized by category.

lines: Core Packets
[msg@"string"] — string literal
[int@42] — numeric literal
[bool@true|false] — boolean literal
[math@expr] — evaluate a math expression
[store@name] — save last value. Modes: rigid, fluid, context(cond)
[var@name] — retrieve a runtime variable
[print] — output last value, pass-through
[dump] — pretty-print last value as JSON, pass-through
[note@"message"] — inline annotation, returns Unit
[len] — length of last value (string, array, or object key count)
[rand] — float in (0,1); [rand(min,max)] for bounded integers
[env@NAME] — read environment variable
[cd@/path] — change working directory within the red box
[parse(json|yaml|toml)@string] — parse string into in-memory document
[array]{ ... } — build an array from enclosed packets
[obj]{ [key(k)@v] ... } — build an object
[reflect(packets)] — introspect canonical packet list
[help@packet] — quick reference for a named packet
[lint@/path/script.tgsk] — flag unsafe usage and TODO markers
[input@"Prompt "] — read a line from stdin

entries.description: Control flow packets: loops, conditionals, functions.
lines: Flow Packets
[funct:tag]{ ... } — define a named reusable block
[call@tag] — invoke a defined function
[loop@N]{ ... } — repeat N times. Sugar: [loop3@tag]
[loop:forever]{ ... } — soft infinite loop, exit via [break] or [return]
[loop:until(condition)]{ ... } — loop until condition is truthy
[loop:each(item@handle)]{ ... } — iterate an array handle
[break] — exit current loop
[return@value] — exit loop or function early
[interrupt@value] — exit loop and raise signal upstream
[if@(cond)]{ ... }[else]{ ... } — conditional dataflow
[or@(cond)] — additional branch in an if-chain
[iter@handle]{ ... } — iterate arrays; sets it and idx
[async]{ ... } — spawn a block without blocking current flow
[async@fn] — spawn a named async function
[await@fn] — wait for async function result
[timeout:unit@len] — pause execution for duration
[interval:unit@len]{ ... } — repeating async timer
Comparators: [eq] [ne] [lt] [le] [gt] [ge] — sugar: == != < <= > >=

entries.description: File I/O packets. All paths sandboxed to red box.
lines: File Packets
[load@/path/file.(json|yaml|toml)] — load file into editable document
[save@handle] — persist document back to original file
[log@/path/file.json] — dump last value as JSON
[log(json|yaml|toml)@/path/file]{ ... } — structured file emit
[mod@handle]{ ... } — mutate a loaded document
Sugar: [set(path)@value] [delete(path)] [insert(path)@value] [append(list)@value] [merge(meta)@{...}]
[get(path)@handle] — extract value at path from document
[exists(path)@handle] — test whether path exists (bool)
All paths resolve inside the nearest red.tgsk root.
Escapes produce E_BOX_VIOLATION. Missing root produces E_BOX_REQUIRED.

entries.description: Exec, network, and consent packets. Opt-in only.
lines: Exec Packets
[exec@"cmd"] — run a shell command, returns stdout
Modes: [exec(code)] [exec(stderr)] [exec(json)]
[run@/path/script.tgsk] — execute another script inside the same red box
[tagspeak:run@/path/script.tgsk] — CLI-flavored wrapper around [run]
[tagspeak:build@/path/script.tgsk] — syntax-check without executing
[http(get|post|put|delete)@url]{ ... } — outbound HTTP, disabled by default
[confirm@"message"]{ ... } — prompt before running a block. Alias: [yellow]
[red@"message"] — enable red-tier ops for this session
[repl(model)]{ ... } — interactive loop, red-only
All exec and network ops are opt-in.
Enable via .tagspeak.toml or env vars: TAGSPEAK_ALLOW_EXEC TAGSPEAK_NET_ENABLED
Time Packets
[UTC] — current UTC timestamp in ISO-8601 format
[UTC@component] — specific UTC component: year month day hour min sec ms unix iso etc.
[local] — current local timestamp in ISO-8601
[local@component] — mirror of UTC but using local clock

entries.description: UI packets for terminal and egui GUI output.
lines: UI Packets
[app@"Title"]{ ... } — top-level UI container (egui window)
[frame:id@"Label"]{ ... } — named structural region
[label@"text"] — text display element
[button@"label"]{ ... } — interactive button with action body
[textbox] / [textedit] — text input elements
[checkbox] — boolean toggle
[separator] / [spacer] — layout dividers
[layout(params)@id] — apply layout to a named region
[layout(params)]{ ... } — inline anonymous layout wrapper
[scope@"name"]{ ... } — UI context capture for scoped state
Layout params: direction spacing padding align width border border_color behavior
Build with --features ui_egui for GUI mode. Console I/O is the default.
[ui:alert@"message"] — show alert, pass through prior value
[ui:select@"opt1|opt2|opt3"] — present menu, return selected option

entries.description: Rust kernel internals. Runtime, AST, values, sandbox.

lines: Kernel: Runtime (runtime.rs)
The Runtime struct owns all execution state: variables, tags, last value, cwd, call depth, async tasks, and the deadman registry.
eval() dispatches Node variants (Chain, Block, Packet, If) and routes packets to their handlers via pattern matching on (namespace, op).
Variables support two modes: direct bindings (vars) and context-aware bindings (ctx_vars) evaluated against a temporary forked runtime.
Async support uses OS threads via fork() — child runtimes inherit vars and tags but get a clean task queue and signal state.
Call depth is capped at 256 by default (TAGSPEAK_MAX_CALL_DEPTH). Exceeding it produces E_CALL_DEPTH_EXCEEDED.
FlowSignal enum (None, Break, Return, Interrupt) propagates control signals up through the eval stack without unwinding.
Kernel: AST (ast.rs)
Node enum: Chain (sequence), Block (grouped), Packet, and If { cond, then_b, else_b }.
Packet struct: optional namespace (ns), op string, optional Arg, optional body.
Arg enum: Str, Ident, Number, CondSrc (raw condition string for if-packets).
BExpr enum: Cmp { lhs, cmp, rhs }, And, Or, Not, Lit (raw chain for runtime eval).
Comparator struct: base (Eq/Lt/Gt), include_eq flag, negate flag — covers all six comparators.
Kernel: Values (values.rs)
Value enum: Unit, Bool(bool), Num(f64), Str(String), Doc(Document).
Document struct: holds a serde_json::Value plus path, extension, mtime, root, and last_json for change tracking.
as_bool() coerces any Value to bool: Unit=false, Num=nonzero, Str=nonempty, Doc=true.
try_num() coerces Num or parseable Str to f64, returns None otherwise.
All values are Clone. Doc carries its sandbox root so file operations can re-validate box membership.
Kernel: fs_guard (fs_guard.rs)
find_root() walks up from a start path looking for a directory containing red.tgsk. Returns the first match.
resolve() normalizes a requested path against the root by walking components and popping on ParentDir.
If the normalized result escapes the root, it bails with E_BOUNDARY_RED.
No symlink resolution is performed — sandbox is path-component based.
Kernel: Config (config.rs)
Config is loaded from .tagspeak.toml in the project root if present, then overridden by env vars.
Fields: allow_exec, exec_allowlist, run_max_depth (default 8), prompts_noninteractive, require_yellow_run, net_enabled, net_allow.
Env vars: TAGSPEAK_ALLOW_EXEC TAGSPEAK_MAX_RUN_DEPTH TAGSPEAK_NONINTERACTIVE TAGSPEAK_EXEC_ALLOWLIST TAGSPEAK_NET_ENABLED TAGSPEAK_NET_ALLOW
Precedence: CLI flags > env vars > .tagspeak.toml > defaults.
TagSpeak Safety Model
Red Box: All file operations are sandboxed to the nearest red.tgsk ancestor. Escapes produce E_BOX_VIOLATION. Missing root produces E_BOX_REQUIRED.
Yellow Gating: [confirm] and [yellow] require explicit user consent before executing a block. Bypass with TAGSPEAK_ALLOW_YELLOW=1.
Exec: Shell commands are opt-in via allow_exec or exec_allowlist in .tagspeak.toml.
Network: HTTP is deny-by-default. Enable via .tagspeak.toml [network] with an explicit allowlist.
Allowlist checks compare parsed URL components (scheme, host, port, path prefix) — not raw string prefix.
URLs with userinfo (user@host) are rejected with E_BOX_VIOLATION to prevent allowlist bypass.
Run Depth: [run] nesting is capped at 8 by default (TAGSPEAK_MAX_RUN_DEPTH).
Call Depth: Recursion capped at 256 (TAGSPEAK_MAX_CALL_DEPTH).
Loop Guard: [loop] capped at 1,000,000 iterations.
Non-Interactive Mode: TAGSPEAK_NONINTERACTIVE=1 disables all prompts; ops default-deny unless explicitly allowed.

entries.description: Fun and gremlin-coded packets. Completely optional. Entirely necessary.
lines: Fun Packets
[PWK] — Power Word Kill. Countdown, ASCII skull, dramatic exit.
[summon@thing] — Attempts to summon a thing. Always fails.
[gecko] — Prints the TagSpeak ASCII banner. 🦎
[please] — Sarcastic response to begging your code to work.
[please:selene] — Flirty approval from Selene. Echoes value with a blessing.
[Deity@name] — Prints a blessing from a named deity.
Special cases: Astarte ('Prepare for war or love.') Set ('Prepare for chaos.')
[Deadman@"message"] — Arms a kill switch. Triggers fatal message if not disarmed before script end.
[disarm] — Disarms the most recently armed Deadman switch.
[alli] — Dev wife message. Outputs: 'Sarym is a smarty pants. ;p'
All fun packets are safe, boxed, and non-networked.
Add them to your scripts for chaos, clarity, or pure gremlin joy.
